about: Contract v2 of ask_salesforce, end to end and model-free (Salesforce conversation memory, stage-2 integration, 2026-11-25).

A made-up three-turn Salesforce chat on the memory fixture of sf_assistant/tests/warehouse_fixture.py: a records question, a follow-up the service answers with a clarifying question (state.pending), then the reply 2.

Per turn: question (as typed), script (the service's scripted model, read only by sf_assistant/tests/test_memory_contract.py), call (the arguments the platform bridge sent, captured by orchestrator/tests/test_sf_memory_contract.py through /chat with SF_ASSISTANT_MEMORY true, the row of the turn before read back from the test PostgreSQL) and reply (the service's result, written by the sf_assistant test from that call with SFA_MEMORY=on).

bridge: the limits, texts and codes the bridge uses (written by the orchestrator test); service: the same for the service (written by the sf_assistant test). Each side checks its own block and the other side's.
Every name and value is made up. request_id is the placeholder req-<turn>; state.made_at is the time the reply was written and is not compared.
regenerate: Only when the contract changes on purpose, in this order, until both tests pass without the switch:

1. orchestrator (guarded harness): wo_env m2_x techsara_m2_x_test -- env SF_MEMORY_CONTRACT_WRITE=1 <orchestrator venv python> -m pytest tests/test_sf_memory_contract.py -q -p no:cacheprovider -p wo_netguard_plugin
2. sf_assistant: SFA_MEMORY_CONTRACT_WRITE=1 PYTHONPATH=src <sf venv python> -m pytest -p no:cacheprovider -q tests/test_memory_contract.py
Each run writes what it can (a call needs the replies of the turns before it; a reply needs its call): three rounds fill an empty fixture.
